profile.reading: Emailage was a Chandler, Arizona-based fraud-prevention and email-risk-scoring software company, acquired by LexisNexis Risk Solutions and now marketed as LexisNexis Emailage. It built analytics software that helps online merchants and financial institutions score transaction risk by email address. It was a software company that ran on cloud and outsourced infrastructure rather than one that operated its own colocation or hosting facility, and a check of the address on file today finds a different, unrelated tenant in place. Nothing publicly available ties this specific address to server or data center infrastructure, and this entry does not present a software company's former office as a data center facility.

reading.body:
Emailage is not a data center and contributes zero megawatts to Arizona's AI infrastructure; it was a fraud-prevention software company whose former Chandler address now houses a different tenant.

The location appears in OpenStreetMap as a data center point, but no published specifications or sources connect the address to server or hosting infrastructure. The current occupant is Safe T Professionals LLC, not Emailage or any operator. This is a misclassification, not a facility.

Arizona has 56 mapped facilities, only 4 with published capacity figures totaling 512 MW. A zero-megawatt former office adds nothing to that count or to the state's compute availability for AI scaling. What the data does not show is whether the building ever held any server equipment; it shows only that no public record ties it to data center operations.
